To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multilayer stacks of niobium oxide based threshold switches show a large voltage extension of their negative differential resistance region as well as a symmetric switching behavior.

the multilayer stacks of niobium oxide based threshold switching devices can be improved by implementing a multilayer stack with optimized layer thicknesses and by applying a high voltage pulse during the forming process.

the application of multistacks consisting of niobiax and niobiumoxide leads to an improvement of the I–V characteristic of the threshold switch in terms of the negative differential region extension, the symmetry of the switching, the stability of the device and a reduction of the forming voltage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the improvement of threshold switching devices by the implementation of multilayer structures.
the optimization of the switching behavior of niobium oxide based threshold switching devices for their application as memristor or selector in neuromorphic and memory applications.
the improvement of niobium oxide based threshold switching devices to enable their integration in neuromorphic systems and in resistive memory circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multilayer stacks can improve the switching characteristics of niobium oxide based threshold switches.
the application of a multilayer stack consisting of a 10 nm thick NbO x /20 nm Nb/20 nm NbO x /5 nm Nb/10 nm NbO 2 stack is the optimal configuration for a threshold switching device.
multilayer stacks are a promising way to improve the properties of the threshold switch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the application of a niobum oxide-based threshold switch is a promising candidate for its use as selector device in bipolar resistive random access memory arrays as well as for its application in oscillating neuromorphic circuits.
the multilayer stacks are a very promising approach for the improvement of the threshold switches and their implementation in neuromorphic and memristive circuits.
the implementation of the multilayer stacks leads to an improved device performance in terms of the switching characteristics, the stability, and the forming voltage.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of a thin niobium oxide switching layer with a thick underlying niobium layer can lead to a significant improvement of the device characteristics, especially the voltage extension of the NDR region and the forming voltage.
the use of multilayer structures allows for a significant improvement of the I–V curve and the device stability.

a multilayer stack consisting of two niobium oxide and one niobium layer can lead to a significant improvement of the I–V behavior of the threshold switching device in terms of the voltage extension of the NDR region, the symmetry of the switching, the forming voltage, the device stability, and the device variability.
